# Plan: drive-lanes

Goal: sofar drive runs N lanes in parallel with conflict-aware orchestration: ready-frontier scheduling, region leases at edit time, a serial merge queue and the record as the shared blackboard. Local worktrees first, then Claude Code cloud sessions. Each step is kept only where it beats serial drive on a fixture (no degradation, in percentages), and a driven task costs fewer tokens than native Claude Code (one session with its own subagents) on the same fixture.

Brief: the operator's words, 1600 chars, verbatim in brief.md; `sofar show brief¶<k>` prints one paragraph.

Progress: 17 done, 3 dropped, 9 remaining

## Phase 3 — Conflict-aware orchestration [active] — 7/10 (3 dropped) done

- [x] 3.1 Region leases at PreToolUse: an Edit's old_string maps to its markdown section or enclosing symbol, else the whole file. An overlap with another lane steers rather than denies, so r4-fixes D17 holds: the hook's context names the holding lane, its task, the region and what is free, and the session works elsewhere or parks (WIP commit, write-back, leases released). Older task wins, so no deadlock; union-merge files never lease. A deny mode sits behind a flag, off, until the operator rules on D17 for driven lanes
- [x] 3.2 Footprint prediction and conflict-aware scheduling: task `touches`, the record's mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. A free lane takes the first ready task that misses every live lease and footprint, else idles; skipped tasks age up
- [x] 3.3 Context packets, deterministic and one line each: lease notice (who holds what, for which task), change brief on merge (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet (own write-back, WIP sha, the brief it waited for)
- [x] 3.4 Measure conflict-aware lanes against naive lanes: merge-conflict rework sessions, parks, lanes busy, wall-clock. Keep each piece only if it improves on 2.5
- [x] 3.5 Peer hint: when 3.1 steers an edit away or 3.3 delivers a lease notice, name the lane holding the region as a reachable Claude Code peer (its SendMessage name from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, through core/peers.ts), so the blocked session can ask it directly. sofar never sends. The hint appears only on a live lease collision; Codex, Cursor and cloud lanes get the record packet alone. Driven `claude -p` sessions already register as peers (verified 2026-10-10: sofar-df was the 1.2 session)
- [-] 3.6 Thread model (D15): a task is a thread, not a session. A retry or a resumed park continues the task's own conversation when the coordinator's resume-or-refresh rule says it pays, else a fresh session takes the 3.3 packet. Each task has an inbox in the record (events addressed to the task id), which hooks deliver at the next tool or prompt boundary. A parked thread is woken only when what it waits on resolves (a lease freed, a dependency merged, CI failed in Phase 4) (dropped)
- [-] 3.7 Thread cost levers (D15). (a) Shared warm prefix: the session-start injection is byte-identical across lanes with per-session lines last, and lane starts are staggered so lanes 2..N read lane 1's cache. (b) Warm-cache scheduling: resume inside the cache TTL, else refresh. (c) Fork at a checkpoint: a retry forks from the end of exploration, not from the failed attempt. (d) A parked thread holds no process. (e) A batched inbox: an FYI packet waits for the next boundary and never wakes a thread. (f) A per-thread context ceiling that hands off instead of compacting (dropped)
- [-] 3.8 Measure threads against fresh sessions on the 1.1 fixture: tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input (from transcripts, never handoff.tokens, which carries the whole session's summed usage, r4-fixes note 01M4K3G1), rework sessions and wall-clock. Keep each 3.7 lever only where it lowers cost with no drop in tasks done or verify pass rate (dropped)
- [x] 3.9 Thread gate, before any thread code (operator 2026-10-11: build threads only once proven efficient; they must save tokens against native workflows). Add `--arm native` to the fixture harness: one Claude Code session drives all 9 fixture tasks with its own subagents, scored on tokens per task split into cache read, cache write and fresh input, tasks done and wall-clock. Then project from the 2.5 reps' transcripts what each retry and park would cost as a warm resume, a cold resume, a checkpoint fork and a fresh 3.3-packet session. 3.6-3.8 go ahead only for the cases where the projection beats both fresh sessions and the native arm; otherwise drop them, citing the numbers
- [x] 3.10 A lane session steered or denied by a lease that sets its task blocked on the holding lane's task is a park, not needs_user: in all 3 of 3.4's leasing reps the agent did that and stopped the run (D37). Close the younger-claims-first gap too (2 of 3 still conflicted). Then re-measure steer against footprint alone on a fixture pair whose footprints miss (a hub both edit outside their titles) before leases can return as a default

## Phase 4 — Below native on tokens [pending] — 0/5 done

> Operator 2026-10-11: "our goal is to use reduced tokens than the native". Ahead of cloud lanes, so the drive takes it first.

- [ ] 4.1 Token anatomy, deterministic, from the 3.4 and 3.9 transcripts: split a driven session's and a native subagent's tokens by source (system prompt and tool schemas, built-in and MCP; the SessionStart injection; each hook's added context; sofar protocol calls and their results; the task's own work; verify runs). results/4.1-anatomy.json ranks the sources by tokens per task and names what 4.2-4.4 must cut to land under native (driven today: 29.6k base, 9.4 calls per task; native subagent: 15.4k, 4.4)
- [ ] 4.2 Lean driven base: a driven session starts at or under a native subagent's base context. The driver hands a task packet (the task, its verify, the decisions and memories that name its files) instead of the full SessionStart digest; per-tool hook context is off in driven sessions unless it carries a rule the edit breaks; the MCP tool list is trimmed to what a driven session calls. Keep only if tasks done and gate pass rate hold
- [ ] 4.3 Bookkeeping by the driver, not the session: the driver records session start, task status and the write-back from what it already sees (the launch, the commit, its own verify, the session's last message), so a driven session spends no calls on the protocol; the prompt names the verify command so the session runs it once before it ends. Target at most 4.4 calls per task
- [ ] 4.4 Cache-shaped launches: every driven session in a run starts on a byte-identical prefix (system, tools, packet frame) with per-task lines last, so session N reads session N-1's cache inside the TTL, and lanes stagger their starts so lanes 2..N read lane 1's. Measure cache write per task against native's 11.8k
- [ ] 4.5 Measure serial and footprint lanes with 4.2-4.4 against native, 3 interleaved reps each on D27's stack. Keep each lever only where it lowers tokens per task (raw and priced) with no drop in tasks done or gate pass. The phase is done only when serial drive sits below native on tokens per task; otherwise name the remaining gap and the next lever as a task
